text:
Tess (PM): Kicking off a quick design review for the new 'Scheduled rotation' feature in Credentials. Figma: https://figma.redwood/keys-rotation-scheduler — want copy, a11y checks, and a11y-safe interactions confirmed. Goal: let orgs schedule automatic rotations (daily/weekly/custom) and preview impact.

Omar (Design): High-level visual notes: 1) the scheduler modal is a lot—cron field, timezone, recurrence presets, and a preview panel. We should simplify presets (Daily / Weekly / Custom) and collapse advanced cron under 'Custom'. 2) Preview should show next 3 rotations with timestamps in user's timezone. 3) Need a clear danger affordance when rotation will invalidate active tokens (warning state).

Riley (Eng): Backend constraints: rotation creates a new key at scheduled time and revokes the old one optionally (checkbox). We can record optional 'grace period' (hours) during which both keys are valid. Important: we must show exactly when existing tokens will stop working. Also note rate-limits when many keys rotate concurrently.

Nina (UX Writer): Copy ideas: modal title: 'Schedule key rotation'. Primary CTA: 'Save schedule'. Secondary: 'Cancel'. Danger checkbox label: 'Revoke old key at rotation time'. Helper line under checkbox: 'Enable a grace period to allow deployments to pick up the new key.' One-line banner for preview: 'Next rotation: Mar 3, 2026 14:00 PDT (in 5 days)'. Long variant for docs: 'When a rotation occurs, a new key is generated and optionally the old key is revoked. Use a grace period to reduce downtime.'

Wei (Accessibility): A11y items: 1) ensure the recurrence presets are buttons with aria-pressed states, keyboard navigable. 2) timezone select must be searchable via keyboard; announce selected tz in SR text. 3) when toggling the revoke checkbox, show an accessible description (aria-live polite) that updates preview of validity window. 4) preview panel should be reachable via tab and its date strings should include ISO in aria-label for clarity.

Omar (Design): Also visual/interaction nit: when a schedule is active show a compact pill in the keys list with next-run time and a small overflow menu to 'Pause' or 'Edit' schedule. Pill color needs to pass contrast. For paused schedules show a muted icon + 'Paused' label and a tooltip explaining 'Paused schedules don't rotate keys until resumed.'

Riley (Eng): Permission model: only users with 'Key Admin' or 'Scheduler' role can create/edit schedules. If a non-authorized user opens modal, show read-only preview with an action 'Request schedule permission' that opens a workspace request flow. The 'Save schedule' control should be disabled with aria-describedby linking to the request explanation.

Nina (UX Writer): Tooltip copy for disabled Save: 'You need the Scheduler role to create rotation schedules. Request access from an org admin.' Short inline microcopy for pill: 'Next rotation: Mar 3, 14:00 PDT'. Compact aria-label for pill: 'Scheduled rotation, next run March 3, 2026 at 14:00 Pacific Daylight Time'.

Wei (Accessibility): Additional: 1) the custom cron input is terrible for SR users. If we keep cron allow a simplified natural-language fallback ("Every day at 2pm"). 2) ensure error states (invalid cron, timezone mismatch) are announced and focus sent to the offending input. 3) when saving, toast should include an accessible link to view the schedule in the key detail panel (aria-describedby).

Omar (Design): Empty-state for schedules list (on key detail): headline 'No rotation scheduled', helper 'Set up automatic rotation to keep keys fresh.' CTA 'Schedule rotation'. Keep illustration minimal and avoid jargon.

Tess (PM): Edge-case question: what about rotating keys that are referenced by other orgs/third-party integrations? We should surface a modal warning: 'This key is used by X services. Rotating may break integrations.' Riley: can we compute referencing services?

Riley (Eng): We have service references in audit logs but it's probabilistic. We can run a best-effort scan and show a count with a caution: 'We detected N references; this may be incomplete.' Also provide a checkbox 'Force rotate even if references detected' gated behind Key Admin permission and with stronger warning copy.

Nina (UX Writer): Strong warning copy variant for force rotate: 'This action may break integrations that use this key. Proceed only if you understand the impact.' Button label for forced action: 'Rotate anyway'. Keep primary path defaulting to non-force.

Wei (Accessibility): For that detected references panel: make the list keyboard navigable, provide SR-only counts and include a link text 'View references' that opens the audit view. If the count is probabilistic, include SR text: 'Reference detection is best-effort and might miss uses.'

scheduler-bot: Schedule feature checklist added: https://figma.redwood/rotation-checklist (presets, timezone handling, preview panel, a11y notes). :white_check_mark:

Tess (PM): Good discussion. Action items: @Omar update Figma to collapse cron under Custom and add preview panel; @Nina provide short/long copy strings and the forced-rotate variants; @Wei run focused a11y pass on the PR; @Riley add backend note about grace period and reference-detection caveat. I'll collect final strings and open the i18n PR. Thanks! :raised_hands:
